newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says tobacco legislation delay to be short.
newsitem.headline: Canada says tobacco legislation delay to be short.

text.p: Canadian Health Minister David Dingwall said on Wednesday that his long-awaited tobacco legislation will be announced "soon" but wouldn't set a specific date.
The legislation was originally slated to be released on Thursday, but the announcement was postponed less than 24 hours before a scheduled news conference.
"All our i's aren't dotted and our t's aren't crossed," Dingwall explained to reporters.

"We're finalizing the package. When the package is ready it will be announced and it will be a comprehensive package which will address all of the issues that I have talked about on many previous occasions," Dingwall said.

Dingwall is expected to introduce new restrictions on tobacco advertising and sponsorship of sporting and cultural events. The Supreme Court struck down a ban on tobacco advertising is September 1995, citing freedom of speech.
There has also been speculation in the Canadian media that the legislation will include a tax hike that would increase the price of cigarettes by C$0.15 cents a pack.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain.

Another major player is Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, owned 60 percent by Rothmans International, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc. A third player is RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
